2609.07153.title: FreqBLiMP: Frequency-Controlled Minimal Pairs Reveal Robustness and Fragility of LLMs Under Lexical Rarity
2609.07153.paper_summary: Minimal-pair benchmarks such as BLiMP evaluate linguistic knowledge by testing whether language models (LMs) prefer acceptable sentences over minimally different unacceptable ones. However, these benchmarks largely ignore lexical frequency variation, despite lexical frequency being a pervasive and highly skewed property of natural language use. Consequently, existing evaluations do not test whether grammatical preferences remain stable when contrasts involve rare lexical items. We introduce FreqBLiMP, a frequency-controlled extension of BLiMP that regenerates all 67 paradigms under explicit Zipf-frequency regimes while preserving each minimal-pair's grammatical contrast. Evaluating multiple open-weight LLM families across scales, we find that decreasing lexical frequency produces a consistent, monotonic decrease in sentence likelihood, but only a modest reduction in overall contrastive acceptability accuracy. However, this aggregate stability masks substantial variation across linguistic phenomena, with LLMs remaining robust on overt morphosyntactic generalization while degrading on phenomena that require lemma-specific information.
2609.07153.paper_summary_zh: 最小對比基準如 BLiMP 通過測試語言模型 (LMs) 是否偏好可接受的句子而非最小不同的不可接受句子來評估語言知識。<lb/>然而，這些基準在很大程度上忽視了詞彙頻率變化，儘管詞彙頻率是自然語言使用中普遍且高度偏斜的特性。<lb/>因此，現有的評估並未測試當對比涉及稀有詞彙項目時，語法偏好是否保持穩定。<lb/>我們引入 FreqBLiMP，這是一個頻率控制的 BLiMP 擴展，能在明確的 Zipf 頻率範疇下重新生成所有 67 種範式，同時保持每對最小對比的語法對比。<lb/>在不同規模的多個開放權重 LLM 家族中進行評估，我們發現降低詞彙頻率會導致句子可能性的一致單調下降，但對整體對比可接受性準確性的減少僅為適度。<lb/>然而，這種整體穩定性掩蓋了語言現象之間的重大變化，LLMs 在明顯的形態句法概括上保持穩健，而在需要詞幹特定信息的現象上則有所退化。
2609.07153.author: Tyrone White et.al.
